speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You have presented with a rash on your scalp and forehead; to begin my assessment, can you describe exactly what the rash looks like, such as whether it is scaly, oozing, crusted, or simply red?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is interesting; the father's history of psoriasis is relevant. Given the patient's age and the rash appearing worse in cold weather, is there any significant family history of atopic dermatitis, or has the rash caused any itching or discomfort to the baby?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Seborrheic Dermatitis. The clinical presentation of erythematous patches with greasy yellow scales on the scalp and forehead, exacerbated by cold weather, in an infant with no significant itching history is classic for this condition, distinguishing it from psoriasis or atopic dermatitis. No further tests are required.
